doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Dream recording project and limits of budgets
summary: She would like to record with the weekend band, and thinks restrictions force craft.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Is there a dream project that you have?
Well after the last couple of nights, I’d like to record with that band. It was great.

We’ll have to do that. A dream project, wow. I mean it’d be nice to have enough of a budget that I could have a great Gospel B3 player on some songs, and a great Gospel choir and somebody playing vibes and somebody with pedal steel. You know it’d be fun to have, not to be at all concerned about the restrictions of money. But on the other hand, same thing, because of those restrictions, you know you have to be more artistic and you have to be, it’s more of a craft, because you have the restrictions.
Yeah. And you think of reading about some of the bands that have these unlimited budgets and they spend four months in the studio.

On one song. Can you imagine? Yeah my sister has played on some of that stuff. I’m not going to call any names, but you know where they put in every note, and of course she was paid very well. And I’m sure she contributed a lot.
